drafted_from: tool:google-account-modify_mail's own row in tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (invoke method, url, body_template, input and output schema); Gmail response values worked out from that row for the synthetic input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Archive message 18c1a2b3d4e5f888 and mark it read. Use my Google account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:google-account-modify_mail as that account and hands back the Gmail answer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls Gmail for one Google account the connection names and answers what Gmail returns.
instructions: 1. Connect a Google account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery.

2. Say to your AI: "Archive message 18c1a2b3d4e5f888 and mark it read." and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:google-account-modify_mail, and the input {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"message_id":"18c1a2b3d4e5f888","remove_label_ids":["INBOX","UNREAD"]}.

3. Read what comes back: the request goes as POST  the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/messages/18c1a2b3d4e5f888/modify with the body {"removeLabelIds":["INBOX","UNREAD"]} (add_label_ids is left out, so addLabelIds is not sent).
4. INBOX archives, UNREAD sets read status, STARRED stars. Use modify_mail_thread for a whole conversation.
